sources.note: Fits a post-hoc sparse autoencoder to the frozen dense tensors that two vision-language agents exchange, finds a 128-fold payload reduction at near-identical reconstruction and roughly unchanged single-run accuracy, and then spends most of the paper enumerating the alternative explanations its own design cannot rule out.
sources.title: Post-Hoc Sparse Coding of Latent Communication Between Vision-Language Model Agents

sources.note: Takes the set of active sparse-autoencoder latents as the unit of analysis and finds that adding a semantically compatible adjective to a noun deactivates 20 to 60 percent of the latents the noun alone had active, which contradicts the bag-of-features reading those sets are usually given.
sources.title: Beyond a Bag of Features: Set-Level Instability in Sparse Autoencoders
